13. Before adverting to the facts of the present case and appreciating the contentions raised, the relevant provisions of law and the essential ingredients that are required to be proved by the prosecution in order to prove the guilt of the accused persons are reproduced herein under:
Section 304B of IPC (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection,
with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called 'dowry death', and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.

(2) ........
Section 498A of IPC:
Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of Shunali a woman,
subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished gupta with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three by Shunali gupta years and shall also be liable to fine.

Explanation- For the purpose of this section, "Cruelty" means- (a) any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health (whether mental or physical) of the woman;
or (b) harassment of the woman where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or is on account of failure by her or any person related to her to meet such demand.
State vs Mohd. Aslam on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12561541/
9 14.

For proving the offence u/s 498A/304B IPC, the prosecution was required to establish that woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment either by husband of the woman or by the relative of the husband.

For the purpose of this section, cruelty means any willful conduct which is of such nature as is likely to drive a woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury to her or where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or is on account of failure by her to make that demand.
Cruelty for the purpose of constituting the offence u/s 498A IPC need not be physical.

Even mental torture tenatamounts to cruelty within the meaning of section 498A IPC.
15.
The prosecution is further required to prove the foundational facts before presumption of law is attracted and the burden of proof is shifted upon the accused.

Presumption under section 113B is a presumption of law that shall be raised only on proof of the following essentials;
(i) The death of a woman must have been caused by burns or bodily injury or otherwise than under normal Shunali circumstances.
gupta (ii) Such death must have occurred within seven years of her marriage.
(iii) The woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relatives.
(iv) Such cruelty or harassment was for, or in connection with any demand for dowry.
(v) The woman is subjected to such cruelty or harassment soon before her death.

16. Now, in light of the above provisions of the law, it has to be seen whether the prosecution has been able to prove that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment by the accused persons after the marriage on account of dowry demands.
17. Analysing the evidence adduced on record.

The prime prosecution witnesses are the parents,
brother and sister of the deceased examined as PW1, PW2, PW4 & PW6.
Apart from that one more independent witness not directly related to the deceased has also been examined as PW3.

However,
in so far as evidence of PW1, PW2, PW4 & PW6 is concerned, all these witnesses have not deposed anything incriminating the accused for the offence of cruelty or demand for dowry.
They have not attributed the cause of death to the accused.
None of these witnesses have deposed that the accused ever demanded dowry from the deceased or from them after the marriage or that he used to harass her.

Thus all these four witnesses have completely turned hostile and exonerated the accused so much so that PW4 has even deposed in his evidence that his sister was kept properly by the accused after the marriage.
Shunali gupta

Coming to the evidence of PW3 during evidence though he has deposed that quarrels and altercations used to take place between deceased and the accused but firstly he was not aware about the issue regarding which the altercation took place and secondly the matter got settled before State vs Mohd. Aslam on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12561541/
10 panchayat as the accused sought apology from the deceased.
Even this witness has not deposed anything about any demand for dowry or any cruelty inflicted upon the deceased on account of the said demand.

As noted earlier, in order to prove the offence of dowry death there has to be clear, categorical and direct allegations of demand of dowry and cruelty inflicted upon the deceased in connection with the said demand.

However, in the present case not only that the allegations of demand for dowry are absolutely absent even there is no deposition vis-a-vis cruelty simplicitor inflicted by the accused upon the deceased.
The only prosecution witness which has deposed regarding cruelty inflicted by the accused is PW3 but his deposition is also confined only to altercations/tu tu main main or beatings to Anjum.

However, his deposition is very cursory - not at all categorical, not given any details about the date or time of incident, the reason for conflict between the accused and deceased or the extent of beatings etc.

Thus such a cryptic and one liner testimony without any material particulars is not at all sufficient to prove the serious allegations of cruelty as envisaged under Section 498A IPC.
18.
As these witnesses were not supporting the prosecution story on any material aspect, they were cross examined by Ld. Addl.PP for the State.

However, even during cross examination Digitally signed by neither of these witnesses deposed anything incriminating the Shunali Shunali gupta gupta Date:
2026.01.29 accused or attributing the cause of death of deceased to the 16:52:37 +0530 accused.
19. Thus, from the evidence of prosecution witnesses PW1, PW2, PW3, PW4 & PW6, it is clear that they have not supported the prosecution case on any material aspect.
Thus, no incriminating evidence has been produced against the accused during the trial which could prove his culpability or connect him to the crime.
It is a settled preposition of criminal law that prosecution is supposed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt by leading cogent, reliable and convincing evidence.
The burden of proof of the version of prosecution in a criminal trial is throughout on the prosecution which the prosecution has failed to discharge.
20. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the prosecution has miserably failed to prove its case that the accused had committed the offences for which he has been charged with.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. Before adverting to the facts of the present case and appreciating the contentions raised, the relevant provisions of law and the essential ingredients that are required to be proved by the prosecution in order to prove the guilt of the accused persons are reproduced herein under:
Section 304B of IPC (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection,
with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called 'dowry death', and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
For proving the offence u/s 498A/304B IPC, the prosecution was required to establish that woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment either by husband of the woman or by the relative of the husband.
For the purpose of this section, cruelty means any willful conduct which is of such nature as is likely to drive a woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury to her or where such harassment is with a view to coercing her or any person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any property or is on account of failure by her to make that demand.
Cruelty for the purpose of constituting the offence u/s 498A IPC need not be physical.
Even mental torture tenatamounts to cruelty within the meaning of section 498A IPC.
15.
The prosecution is further required to prove the foundational facts before presumption of law is attracted and the burden of proof is shifted upon the accused.
Presumption under section 113B is a presumption of law that shall be raised only on proof of the following essentials;
(i) The death of a woman must have been caused by burns or bodily injury or otherwise than under normal Shunali circumstances.
gupta (ii) Such death must have occurred within seven years of her marriage.
(iii) The woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or his relatives.
(iv) Such cruelty or harassment was for, or in connection with any demand for dowry.
(v) The woman is subjected to such cruelty or harassment soon before her death.
16. Now, in light of the above provisions of the law, it has to be seen whether the prosecution has been able to prove that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment by the accused persons after the marriage on account of dowry demands.
Apart from that one more independent witness not directly related to the deceased has also been examined as PW3.
They have not attributed the cause of death to the accused.
Even this witness has not deposed anything about any demand for dowry or any cruelty inflicted upon the deceased on account of the said demand.
As noted earlier, in order to prove the offence of dowry death there has to be clear, categorical and direct allegations of demand of dowry and cruelty inflicted upon the deceased in connection with the said demand.
However, in the present case not only that the allegations of demand for dowry are absolutely absent even there is no deposition vis-a-vis cruelty simplicitor inflicted by the accused upon the deceased.
The only prosecution witness which has deposed regarding cruelty inflicted by the accused is PW3 but his deposition is also confined only to altercations/tu tu main main or beatings to Anjum.
However, his deposition is very cursory - not at all categorical, not given any details about the date or time of incident, the reason for conflict between the accused and deceased or the extent of beatings etc.
Thus such a cryptic and one liner testimony without any material particulars is not at all sufficient to prove the serious allegations of cruelty as envisaged under Section 498A IPC.
18.
As these witnesses were not supporting the prosecution story on any material aspect, they were cross examined by Ld. Addl.PP for the State.
However, even during cross examination Digitally signed by neither of these witnesses deposed anything incriminating the Shunali Shunali gupta gupta Date:
2026.01.29 accused or attributing the cause of death of deceased to the 16:52:37 +0530 accused.
19. Thus, from the evidence of prosecution witnesses PW1, PW2, PW3, PW4 & PW6, it is clear that they have not supported the prosecution case on any material aspect.
Thus, no incriminating evidence has been produced against the accused during the trial which could prove his culpability or connect him to the crime.
It is a settled preposition of criminal law that prosecution is supposed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt by leading cogent, reliable and convincing evidence.
The burden of proof of the version of prosecution in a criminal trial is throughout on the prosecution which the prosecution has failed to discharge.
